Decided to look into it. The first thing I found was that both the Cascades and Ricky were active at the same time. However, in 1962 when the Cascades released this, from 1957 to 1962, Nelson had 30 Top-40 hits. Why would he record with a then unknown group? The Cascades were signed to Valiant Records and Ricky signed a 20 year contract with Decca that year (more later). The only connection I could find is Phil Spector:

In the Summer of 1962 they did some recording at the legendary Gold Star Studios in Los Angeles, which was record producer Phil Spector's favorite recording studio. In those days groups would often go to the studio to record a single song rather than a whole album. One day the Cascades went to Gold Star and recorded Gummoe's composition of Rhythm Of The Rain, with John Gummoe on lead vocals. Spector happened to be in the studio at the time of the session and asked them if they were recording a demo for Ricky Nelson.

Admittedly, the vocals on Rhythm do sound a LOT like Ricky. In fact compare the Cascades first release The Last Leaf and For Your Sweet Love (done the same year), the lead vocals are definitely different than Rhythm. Both are the same guy John Gummoe. Listening to those it's hard to say Ricky didn't do Rhythm just by ear. I guess it's possible Ricky did sing it just prior, or maybe to interest, Decca into his new contract and Decca wouldn't let this be known he sang on it because he hadn't signed yet and Decca wouldn't get the royalties.

If I had to guess, I'd say yes, it was Ricky on Rhythm. Mainly due to the difference of vocals on the other 2 vocals on the Cascades records recorded around, or at, the same relative time. It's just too stark a difference. Add in my conjecture about Ricky wanting/getting a huge contract with a major label, it seems very likely. Ricky is dead and John is still alive.
